correctness.rationale: For n>=1 and the specified regular polarization, the permutohedron is the sum of [e_i,e_j] over i<j on n+1 coordinates: a strict ordering of the objective chooses one endpoint for each edge and yields precisely a permutation of 0,...,n. Differences generate the lattice A_n. A maximal set of edge differences has determinant of magnitude one in A_n when the edges form a spanning tree (integral path differences give a basis) and zero otherwise. Consequently the lattice-covolume volume counts (n+1)^(n-1) trees. The Ehrhart leading coefficient gives degree n! times that volume. By the torus-orbit stratification, positive-dimensional complex tori contribute zero Euler characteristic and the (n+1)! maximal cones contribute one each. The quotient is (n+1)^(n-2), giving 1/2, 1, and >1 respectively at n=1, n=2, n>=3, with both invariants 6 for the hexagonal del Pezzo surface. The comparison is of n! times the tree count with the permutation count, not the two bare counts; in dimension two the latter are 3 and 6. The unique-equality statement is for positive dimensions as in the stated classification.
